sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar for Shabbos Eikev, 20 Menachem Av 5723.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos of the portion of Eikev,
20 Menachem-Av, 5723*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the apparent contradiction of the manna being described as affliction and hunger, and explains the difference between the blessing of "Hazan" instituted by Moshe for the manna and the blessing of "Al HaAretz" for bread from the land.

translations.translation: "And He afflicted you and made you hungry and fed you the manna..."1,
And the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory, in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh"2,
[notes] that everywhere else in the Torah it speaks of the virtue of the manna,
but here it says "And He afflicted you and made you hungry..." which is seemingly the opposite of virtue.
Also, one must understand that it is stated in the Gemara3
Moshe instituted for Israel the blessing of "Hazan" at the time that the manna descended for them,
Yehoshua instituted for them the blessing of "Al HaAretz" when they entered the land.
And the Rashba wrote4
that the explanation of "Moshe instituted... Yehoshua instituted..."5
is that they established for them the formula of the blessings,
for the blessings themselves are from the Torah
[as it is stated in the Gemara3,
"And you shall eat and be satisfied and bless"6
— this is the blessing of "Hazan"... "upon the land" — this is the blessing of "Al HaAretz"].
And it is stated in Likkutei Torah7,
that the reason that in the blessing of "Al HaAretz" we also mention "upon the eating of food" and in the sealing of the blessing we seal "upon the land and upon the food"
(even though we have already recited the blessing of "Hazan"),
is,
because the wording and formula of the blessing of "Hazan" is for the manna,
bread from the heavens,
and the food in the blessing of "Al HaAretz" is bread from the land8.
And explanation is needed,
for the blessing of "Hazan" is for eating that satisfies
("And you shall eat and be satisfied"),
and eating that satisfies is
(primarily)
with bread from the land,
and nevertheless,
the blessing for the food of bread from the land is in the blessing of "Al HaAretz"
(in which "And you shall eat and be satisfied" is not stated9),
and the wording of the blessing of "Hazan"
(in which "And you shall eat and be satisfied" is written)
is for the manna, about which it is written "And He afflicted you and made you hungry"10.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions the comparison of the affliction of hunger from the manna to the affliction of Yom Kippur, and notes that the blessing of "Hazan" instituted by Moshe for the manna is still recited today for bread from the land.

translations.translation: Also, one must understand that the affliction of Yom Kippur is derived11
from the affliction stated regarding the manna,
[for] affliction is stated here
("And you shall afflict your souls"12)
and affliction is stated there
("And He afflicted you and made you hungry")
[so] just as there the affliction is of hunger, so too here the affliction is of hunger.
And explanation is needed,
for the affliction of hunger of the manna is that eating the manna did not satisfy them as fully needed
[for one who has bread in his basket is not comparable to one who does not have bread in his basket11
(and the manna was a thing13
day by day14)
and one who sees and eats is not comparable to one who does not see and eats11
(and with the manna they tasted all kinds but did not see anything but manna14)],
and from this that they compare the affliction of hunger of the manna to the affliction of hunger of Yom Kippur,
it implies,
that the affliction of hunger of the manna is
(not that eating the manna did not satisfy like eating in the usual manner,
but rather)
like one who did not eat15.
And it is noteworthy,
that based on this, one must understand even more that the wording of the blessing of "Hazan" is for the manna.
Also, one must understand16,
that now
(after the manna ceased),
all the blessings of Grace After Meals are seemingly for bread from the land,
and nevertheless the wording of the blessing of "Hazan" is the wording that Moshe instituted for the manna.
